newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Cacao de Zaan seen untouched by Grace sale.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Cacao de Zaan seen untouched by Grace sale.

text.p: Production at one of the largest Dutch cocoa grinders, Cacao de Zaan, is not in danger following the decision by its ultimate parent W.R. Grace & Co to spin off its Grace Cocoa unit, sources said.
They said a buyer was expected to be found for the entire division but that one of two possible scenarios could follow.

"Either the whole unit (Grace Cocoa) could be absorbed by another large cocoa player or that could be broken up and Cacao de Zaan could be sold separately," one said. "But either way, there is no danger to production at Cacoa de Zaan."
Noone was availble at Cacao de Zaan to comment.
W.R. Grace said earlier this week it would spin-off non-core operations, which included U.S.-based Grace Cocoa. Sources here said they expected a deal to be finalised by the year-end.
Analysts have in the past linked the U.S. trade house Cargill with a possible purchase of Grace Cocoa. As far back as 1993, W.R. Grace & Co said it wanted to sell Grace Cocoa.

The company grinds around 260,000 tonnes of beans a year at factories in eight countries. Much of its cocoa comes from the Ivory Coast, where it took a 30 percent stake in February this year in major cocoa and coffee exporter SIFCA.
